intro: In the Tektek Mountains of Şanlıurfa province lies Soğmatar, a sanctuary of the 2nd century AD – 7th century AD. Here, a sacred hill and rock tombs were dedicated to the moon god Sin.
history: In the 2nd century AD, under the Abgar dynasty, this was a cult centre where the people of Harran worshipped the moon and the planetary gods. As you explore, you will find the Pognon Cave, a Sacred Hill with reliefs of deities, and six mausolea.
structure-1: You are now at the Pognon Cave, the sacred cave of Soğmatar, dedicated to the moon god Sin. Step closer and feel the stillness of this place of worship.
structure-2: Look now at the Sacred Hill Reliefs. Here on the Sacred Hill at Soğmatar, reliefs depict the deities. Take your time to make out their forms.
structure-3: These are the Mausolea, monumental tombs dedicated to the city's leading figures. Pause and think of the people they were built to remember.
structure-5: And here is the Moses Well. Local tradition at Soğmatar attributes this well to the Prophet Moses.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Rock-cut Tombs.
facts: Did you know? Local tradition holds that the Prophet Moses lived here, and his well is still visited today. Soğmatar was an open-air sanctuary of the planets and of the moon god Sin, and Syriac inscriptions were cut into its rock in the second and third centuries AD. Around the central sacred hill, seven separate structures are thought to be scattered, one for each planet.
outro: This brings our journey through Soğmatar to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. These stones have waited for centuries; let them keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
